mechanism_narrative: The observed slight upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks, despite overall low levels, indicates a nascent recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating the recovery was temporary or stalled.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility, as seen at t-0w, signals a growing public comfort with outdoor activities and public spaces, which will translate into increased RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks if PARKS remains above -40% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility fails to remain above -40% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next two weeks despite PARKS meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a return to daily commuting patterns, which directly increases foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT mobility declines or stagnates, or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite both proxies showing sustained recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are staying home. If this trend reverses and RESIDENTIAL falls below 16%, it will free up time and opportunity for out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 16% or increases, or RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days even if RESIDENTIAL falls below 16%.

mechanism_narrative: Despite minor fluctuations, RETAIL_REC remains at severely suppressed levels (around -60% of baseline), indicating deeply ingrained behavioral changes and ongoing constraints that will prevent significant recovery, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a significant break from the suppressed state.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, a more essential category, would signal a broader contraction in all non-residential movement due to heightened caution or perceived risk, leading to a decrease in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not fall by more than 2 points week-on-week, or RETAIL_REC increases over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues to rise while WORKPLACES mobility remains stagnant or declines, it indicates a preference for outdoor leisure activities over work-related outings, potentially diverting discretionary time and spending away from traditional retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks while PARKS rises and WORKPLACES stagnates or declines, suggesting leisure activity does not divert from retail.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 17% and a decline in TRANSIT mobility below -60% would signal a public perception of tightening restrictions or increased risk, leading to a further reduction in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 17% and TRANSIT falls below -60%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL rising above 17% and TRANSIT falling below -60%, or these conditions are not met.
